title: fix(plugins): preserve CLI environment and worker test routing
body:
## What Problem This Solves

CLI backend descriptor and ID lookups accepted an explicit environment but dropped it when evaluating installed-plugin activation. A lookup prepared for a custom state directory could therefore use the process directory’s bundled-discovery policy and incorrectly hide an available backend.

## What Changed

Forward the existing environment to the existing activation predicate in both lookup paths. Policy, cache lifetime, public signatures, and persisted state stay unchanged.

Complete the related test-routing cutover for six remaining consumers that perform real worker-backed model preparation. They use the existing forked database-worker project; media routing remains exclusive, and the simple-completion fixture retains its existing compiled-runtime prerequisite. The already-landed CLI validation and TTS selection entries are preserved. No test bodies, admission guard, or assertions are weakened.

## Evidence

- The real two-root regression fails on original production because the compatibility-root lookup returns no backend. The candidate passes all 11 descriptor cases, including interleaved root selection and zero host SQLite during prepared lookups. The new case took 929 ms; the full file took 35.12 s including the wrapper, dominated by transformation.
- The unchanged config-validation case reproduced the host-broker refusal on its old CLI thread route. The maintained fork route passes the whole 23-case file; six related files pass 82 cases, and the compiled simple-completion file passes seven more after a clean normal runtime build. These are scoped runs, not one combined suite.
- Normal runtime build passed, including 53 built-module/native-require and Doctor-closure checks. Core/test types, scripts/root types, type-aware lint, formatting, Knip, schema guards, and runtime-cycle checks passed through the relevant changed-file gates. Independent review of the five-file source is clean through P2. Follow-up review caught a partial-setup cleanup gap in the new test; both roots now use the existing temporary-directory tracker, with exact database handles closed before removal. The same 11 cases pass and the correction has a fresh P3 review.

No configuration or storage migration is required.

## CI attribution

The initial head’s [CI attempt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36595670704) failed the production-suppression scanner on an unchanged MCP test helper (expected 77, observed 78). The scanner/helper inputs match the tested baseline, and the independently qualified [canonical correction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1d0efa48d3a842cf0a86164cf6e37f4db2e457ae) removes that suppression. The fail-fast monitor cancelled 68 other jobs; their coverage is not reported as passing. This attribution belongs to head `029e7044`; successor-head CI is tracked separately.

The corrected head `c3a87c25` has a separate [failed CI attempt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36603564463): the package-admission fixture still expects 76 Docker groups after the intentional [stable-profile aggregate removal](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e89ae266d753c55f127f4235adda7f24fe6c7fc1) reduced the plan to 75. All 12 decisive fixture/planner inputs match the tested baseline and merge. Independent main reproduces the failure; restoring only the removed membership makes the unchanged bounded-record test pass. The independent [fixture correction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7098bf6cddd8cda57ea1f78083546968f299538c) now validates selection completeness while preserving the byte limit, digests, status and no-side-effect assertions. Native pre-existing-CI admission retains this failed result and the 62 fail-fast cancellations as unrun coverage; security passed. The exact-head follow-up review reports no actionable findings.

### Post-merge routing correction

Main had independently registered the PDF resource test in `16b17b22` before this PR merged. Combining the two additions left a duplicate inventory entry and blocked a later CI preflight. [Canonical correction `b4df789c`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b4df789c4a95f9b2b8f4290e47d7355efcc71f48) removes only the duplicate, preserving the forked route and strict timing guard. The existing registry/planner checks pass, with 853 unique inventory entries and one PDF route. The earlier branch proof did not cover this later merge interaction.
